title: Tech Note: Understanding Cyclic Redundancy Check

historical_commentary.text: CRC remains a fundamental concept in data integrity and communications, used in everything from network protocols to file systems. The 4D-specific implementation code from 1999 would need updating for modern 4D syntax, but the underlying theory explained in this note is timeless. Modern 4D provides built-in hashing functions (like Generate digest) that handle many use cases where CRC was once manually implemented, but understanding CRC theory remains valuable for developers working with low-level data validation.
related_updates: Modern 4D includes built-in Generate digest command supporting MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and other hash algorithms
CRC-32 is still widely used in ZIP files, PNG images, Ethernet frames, and many protocols
The theoretical concepts of polynomial division and binary arithmetic for CRC remain unchanged
